evidence.title: Canada's public broadcaster changes policy that said not to label 9/11 attacks 'terrorism'

occurrences.checkable_against: CBC memo and journalistic standards policies of the cited organizations
occurrences.quote_span: She said the memo “was a reminder of the long-standing practice that favors the use of these terms with attribution in our reporting, a practice shared by many of the world’s top journalistic organizations.”
occurrences.speaker: Kerry Kelly
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: CBC memo and Warren Kinsella's Toronto Sun report
occurrences.quote_span: The fracas began after Toronto Sun columnist Warren Kinsella reported on a memo, in which he said CBC News staff were told “do not refer to the Sept. 11 attacks as terrorist attacks.”
occurrences.speaker: Warren Kinsella
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: Public post by the Republican congressional representatives
occurrences.quote_span: A group of Republican representatives in Congress also posted earlier in the day: “What possible motive could there be for sanitizing the worst terrorist attack on American soil? Care to explain, @Canada?”
occurrences.speaker: Republican representatives in Congress
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: CBC/Radio-Canada reporting standards and subsequent CBC coverage
occurrences.quote_span: “At the same time, as new acts of politically or ideologically motivated violence occur in our world, we will continue to follow the journalistically sound practice of attributing causes and motivations to officials and experts.”
occurrences.speaker: Basem Boshra
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: Kerry Kelly statement to The Canadian Press
occurrences.quote_span: CBC spokesperson Kerry Kelly told the The Canadian Press that it was the public broadcaster’s practice to use “extreme caution” in using the words terrorism or terrorist.
occurrences.speaker: Kerry Kelly
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: CBC/Radio-Canada standards announcement or statement on 9/11 terminology
occurrences.quote_span: Canada’s public broadcaster said Friday it is making an exception to its policy of not labeling specific attacks as terrorism for the 9/11 attacks after coming under fire over a memo restating it.
occurrences.speaker: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: Public statements by the named officials, congressional members and Conservative Party; CBC staff memo
occurrences.quote_span: But the director of the FBI, the U.S. ambassador to Canada, Republican members of Congress and Canada’s Conservative party all criticized the CBC following media reports about a memo reminding journalists of the policy sent to staff ahead of the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 attacks .
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: Kash Patel's public online post
occurrences.quote_span: “Any agency in Canada that doesn’t publicly reject this bastardization of history, and an insult to the souls lost during our largest terrorist attack in U.S. history will no longer have friend in this FBI,” FBI Director Kash Patel said an online post late Thursday.
occurrences.speaker: Kash Patel
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: The Canadian Press correspondence with CBC spokesperson Kerry Kelly
occurrences.quote_span: Kelly did not provide a copy of the memo.
occurrences.speaker: Kerry Kelly
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: Brodie Fenlon's 2023 CBC blog post and the cited organizations' style policies
occurrences.quote_span: “Attribution of the word ‘terrorist’ has been our policy for decades — mirrored by other news organizations such as the BBC, AP, AFP and Reuters, among many others,” Fenlon wrote.
occurrences.speaker: Brodie Fenlon
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: FBI operational and disruption records for Canada in 2026
occurrences.quote_span: the FBI has been responsible or instrumental in disrupting terrorist and violent criminal organizations operating in Canada multiple times this year.
occurrences.speaker: Pete Hoekstra
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: Brodie Fenlon's 2023 CBC blog post
occurrences.quote_span: the outlet often uses the word terrorist, but with attribution.
occurrences.speaker: Brodie Fenlon
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: Pete Hoekstra's social-media post and FBI operational records for Canada in 2026
occurrences.quote_span: On Friday, U.S. Ambassador to Canada Pete Hoekstra weighed in, sharing Patel’s post and saying the FBI has been responsible or instrumental in disrupting terrorist and violent criminal organizations operating in Canada multiple times this year.
occurrences.speaker: Pete Hoekstra
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: CBC blog post by Basem Boshra dated August 28, 2026
occurrences.quote_span: “We are doing so to remove what has unfortunately (and unintentionally) become an impediment to clarity and public understanding,” he said.
occurrences.speaker: Basem Boshra
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: CBC News coverage and the 9/11 Commission Report
occurrences.quote_span: We have reported fully and accurately on the reasons and motivations for those attacks as determined by police, governments and an independent commission.
occurrences.speaker: Basem Boshra
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: Marc Miller's social-media post about CBC's policy change
occurrences.quote_span: Canada’s Culture Minister Marc Miller praised the move on social media, calling it a “welcome change to what was a piece of pedantic and foolish guidance that caused legitimate anger.”
occurrences.speaker: Marc Miller
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: CBC News archives and Basem Boshra's blog post
occurrences.quote_span: In the post, Boshra said CBC News “has never said what happened on Sept. 11, 2001, was not terrorism, as some commentators have stated in recent days.
occurrences.speaker: Basem Boshra
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: Public Safety Canada press release by Gary Anandasangaree dated August 28, 2026
occurrences.quote_span: Boshra’s post was published less than an hour after Public Safety Minister Gary Anandasangaree issued a press release saying the Canadian government “has always recognized 9/11 as the deadliest terrorist attack in history, and we unequivocally condemn terrorism in all its forms.”
occurrences.speaker: Gary Anandasangaree / Government of Canada
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: CBC blog post by Basem Boshra dated August 28, 2026
occurrences.quote_span: Basem Boshra, senior director of journalistic standards and public trust, said in a blog post late Friday afternoon that CBC would make an exception to the rule for the 9/11 attacks.
occurrences.speaker: Basem Boshra
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation

occurrences.checkable_against: Pete Hoekstra's public statement
occurrences.quote_span: Hoekstra added: “Failure to recognize and confront radical and terrorist ideologies significantly endangers our efforts to establish and harmonize a shared national and economic security partnership.”
occurrences.speaker: Pete Hoekstra
occurrences.subject: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation
